answer_summary: Under the standard fixed-temperature, fixed-pressure spontaneous-reaction interpretation, tick the bottom-right (third-row, right-column) graph: dG/dt remains nonpositive, oscillates with decaying amplitude, and tends to zero from below.
assumptions: The standard Gibbs-energy criterion applies: the closed system evolves spontaneously at fixed temperature and pressure with no non-expansion work, so Gibbs energy is nonincreasing.
The finite reacting system has Gibbs energy bounded below and relaxes toward equilibrium.
The source phrase oscillatory reaction is represented qualitatively by an oscillatory Gibbs-dissipation rate; no numerical period or amplitude is assumed.
source_gaps: The problem says closed but does not explicitly state fixed temperature and pressure or the absence of non-expansion work; closedness alone is insufficient for an unconditional dG/dt <= 0 claim.

The problem supplies no concrete differentiable time law. The continuous Lean theorem therefore keeps differentiability, rate oscillation, and relaxation to zero as explicit model premises; a separate discrete theorem derives the analogous sign and limiting facts from monotonicity and a lower bound without inventing a kinetic function.
